study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Tabbal et al., npj Parkinson's Disease, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) implemented using the gamlss R package. The models used fractional polynomials as smoothing functions to accommodate nonlinearity. Different distribution families (SEP4, GG, ST3, SEP3, ST1) were selected based on BIC scores for different features and frequency bands.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To estimate the normative age-related curves for EEG spectral power and functional connectivity (as response variables), we implemented the Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) using the gamlss package.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Two main EEG-derived features were used as response variables: (1) Relative EEG spectral power computed at scalp electrodes across frequency bands (delta [1-4 Hz], theta [4-8 Hz], alpha [8-13 Hz], beta [13-30 Hz], gamma [30-45 Hz]) using Welch's method; (2) EEG source-level functional connectivity computed using amplitude envelope correlation (AEC) between 68 cortical regions defined by the Desikan-Killiany atlas, with pairwise orthogonalization applied.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we selected EEG relative spectral power and functional source connectome across standard frequency bands from delta to gamma as response variables for the normative models due to their notable prevalence in the EEG literature
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Discussion (paragraph 2) and Methods / Scalp-level spectral features / Source-level functional connectivity features

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was the main covariate, modeled using fractional polynomials (fp(age, 1)) to capture non-linear age effects. Sex was included as a factor in some models (specifically for delta band functional connectivity). Site was evaluated as both fixed and random effect and included based on BIC comparison. The final model structure varied by feature and frequency band - for spectral features: mu ~ fp(age, 1), sigma ~ 1; for FC features: mu ~ fp(age, 1) or fp(age, 1) + factor(sex) for delta band, sigma ~ fp(age, 1).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, our response variable is an EEG-derived feature, and age serves as the main covariate. The inclusion of other covariates such as sex and data collection sites is detailed in subsequent sections. Following Bethlehem et al., we used fractional polynomials as a smoothing function to accommodate nonlinearity while maintaining model stability.
